newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Central Bank to ease capital inflow rules.
newsitem.headline: Russian Central Bank to ease capital inflow rules.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank will act on its own and with the lower house of parliament to amend laws to ease restrictions on bringing capital into Russia, the Central Bank chairman said on Tuesday.
"Capital should be brought in freely," Sergei Dubinin told a bankers association.
"Until special legislation is passed, the Central Bank will make its own instructions which will make it easier to receive capital from abroad," he said.
"Ideally, we are trying to generally discontinue licensing the majority of these operations," he said.
He said that the bank and the State Duma lower house of parliament were working on changes to the law on hard currency control which would ease capital inflow restrictions.

The Central Bank has set a timetable to do away with restrictions on repatriating funds invested in the government securities market, which is required by the International Monetay Fund charter which Russia has signed.
The bank says it needs the ability to limit inflows to defend against sudden capital flight, though it encourages foreign investment.
